questions.question: In the module pattern IIFE example, why is `count` truly private rather than just a naming convention?
options: Because it's declared with const instead of let
Because it only exists inside the closure created by the IIFE, and the returned object never exposes a reference to it
Because it starts with an underscore
JavaScript doesn't actually support private state at all
questions.explanation: The variable lives only inside the IIFE's scope; since the returned object doesn't expose it directly, there is no way to reach it from outside — true closure-based encapsulation.

questions.question: What guarantee does the Singleton pattern provide?
options: That a function can only be called once
That only one instance of a class/resource exists, with every subsequent construction attempt returning that same instance
That the class cannot be extended
That the class has no constructor
questions.explanation: A singleton ensures a single shared instance app-wide, which the Database example achieves by returning the existing instance from the constructor if one was already created.

questions.question: In the observer/pub-sub pattern, what is the key benefit of the publisher not knowing who's subscribed?
options: It makes the code run faster
It decouples the event source from its consumers, so subscribers can be added or removed independently without the publisher needing any changes
It prevents more than one listener from ever being registered
It removes the need for functions entirely
questions.explanation: Decoupling publisher from subscriber is the whole point of pub-sub — the emitter just broadcasts, and any number of independent listeners can react without it knowing anything about them.

questions.question: Why does `bus.on(...)` return a function in the EventEmitter example?
options: To provide a convenient way to unsubscribe that specific listener later, without needing to keep a separate reference to the original callback
It's a mistake — on() should return nothing
To allow chaining multiple .on() calls together
questions.explanation: Returning an unsubscribe closure is a common ergonomic pattern — the caller can call the returned function later to remove exactly that listener.
